body:
`person:group-hcl-nadar` · flag: **clean** · confidence: verified · tickers: HCLTECH

Flag: CLEAN (HCL Tech) with a legacy blemish (HCL Infosystems). HCL Technologies (promoter ~60%) has been a high-payout company: quarterly dividends with a stated ~75%+ payout policy and occasional buybacks; no promoter pledging; no SEBI findings against promoters. Succession was handled in steps: Roshni Nadar Malhotra became chair of HCL Tech (2020), and by gift deeds of 6-Mar-2025 Shiv Nadar gave her 47% of promoter vehicles Vama Sundari Investments (Delhi) and HCL Corp (his stake 51% -> 4%; hers 10.33% -> ~57.3%), giving her voting control of ~44.3% of HCL Tech; SEBI exempted the open offer and total promoter holding stayed ~60.8%. Legacy blemish: HCL Infosystems (hardware/distribution) shrank into heavy losses through the 2010s, eroding its minority shareholders' value; it was eventually wound into the group (details unverified). HCL Tech's large IBM software IP purchase (2019, $1.8bn) was a capital-allocation debate, not a governance breach. Investor read: one of the cleaner promoter-led IT names; the payout policy is the key minority protection.

- **red flags:** HCL Infosystems value erosion (legacy)
- **good conduct:** high dividend payout; clean succession

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:INDOTECH:promoter-pledge-reduced-by-mar27`
- **Method:** flags-judgment context · **P(ours)** 0.20 · **P(base)** 0.30 · resolve by 2027-04-30
- **Evidence:** NSE pledge data (broadcast 20-Nov-2026, SHP 30-Sep-2026): promoter holding 70.29% of 1.062 cr shares; 82.41% of promoter shares encumbered = 57.93% of total. Pledges/encumbrances in favour of trustees (Catalyst Trusteeship, SBICAP Trustee) on behalf of the promoter Shirdi Sai Electricals (SSEL)'s lenders since Oct–Nov 2025; SSEL sold shares on the open market on 29–30 Jun 2026. memdb event:INDOTECH:avoid-2026-11-19 flags this as a red flag.
- **Why our number differs from base:** The encumbrance secures the promoter group's own borrowings (not a margin loan), which tends to persist until the group refinances; open-market sales by the promoter suggest liquidity need, not release. Flags-judgment: this flag has a verifiable mechanism (lender security), so we expect it to stay.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Indian promoter pledges above 50% of total equity are reduced within ~6 months roughly 30% of the time.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if the NSE pledge/encumbrance disclosure for the 31-Mar-2027 shareholding pattern shows promoter shares pledged/encumbered as % of total shares < 57.93% (a fall caused only by the promoter selling pledged shares still counts as YES; any increase or no change = NO).
- **Resolution source:** NSE corporate pledge data (tools/nse_fetch.py pledge INDOTECH), SHP for quarter ended 31-Mar-2027
- **Sources used:** https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-pledged-data (via tools/nse_fetch.py pledge INDOTECH, 20-Nov-2026); https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-sast-regulations (via tools/nse_fetch.py sast INDOTECH)

body:
Enough data exists for the outcome side of an Indian re-test. **IBBI's public-announcement export is the key
source**: every CIRP admission since January 2017 with the debtor's CIN, which marks listed companies. Exchange
lists give identifiers (ISIN, BSE code, NSE symbol) but few dates. Two gaps remain:
(1) an admission is not a death (see the caveats: Inox Wind and VA Tech Wabag both appear in 2017);
(2) point-in-time *financials* for the dead firms (screener keeps pages for many delisted companies; still to test).
